answers.answer: 1. Starting money: each player takes 25 money. 2. Workers: each starts with 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the reserve spaces below it. 3. Zoo cards: draw 8, keep 4 as hand cards, and discard the other 4 face up. 4. Final Scoring cards: draw 2 and keep them hidden beside the zoo map. 5. Action cards: place Animals side I in the leftmost slot (strength 1); shuffle the other four Action cards among the remaining slots, all side I up. 6. Appeal by turn order: start player on 0, second on 1, third on 2, fourth on 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C–F: 1 active and 3 inactive workers; 25 money; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4; Animals in slot 1; Appeal track staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. Two players: put 3 Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; block the left level on the left card, middle level on the middle card, and right level on the right card. Also block the three spaces in the left donation-area column. 2. Three players: put 3 base projects face up; none of their levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup. 3. Four players: put 4 base projects face up; none of their levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup. 4. Initial display: deal 6 Zoo cards face down during global setup, but reveal those six only after every player has chosen and retained their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c states the 4-player/otherwise project counts and 2-player blocking; Personal setup G says reveal the display after hand selection.

answers.answer: 1. After using a card from slot 4, remove it, slide the cards that were to its left one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before carrying out the action; each X-token spent then adds 1 strength. 3. X-tokens can raise strength, but above strength 5 some actions gain no further benefit; X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. 4. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 5. Resolve an “after finishing” effect only after the action is complete, including the Action-card movement.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “set the strength before performing the action”; each X-token adds +1; max 5; after-finishing effects follow moving the card.

answers.answer: 1. No: you may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; you must perform something, or choose the X-token alternative if unable or unwilling to do a regular action. 2. For that alternative, select an Action card, move it to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right, then take exactly 1 X-token; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take this action while already holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says zero animals/buildings is not legal; X-token action says take exactly 1, move a card to slot 1, and it is unavailable at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, the break occurs after the current turn; disregard movement steps beyond the last space. 2. The player who reaches the last space gains 1 X-token. 3. The triggering player completes the current turn, including the remainder of the action and its turn-end effects, before the break. 4. After the break, return the Break token to the starting space for the player count; play proceeds clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: break after end of current turn, gain 1 X-token, ignore additional steps; after break token returns to start and play continues clockwise with next player.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I: first advance the Break token 2 spaces without money, then choose either a deck draw according to strength (maximum 3, with a possible discard) or a snap. 2. Cards I snap requires strength 5 or more and takes exactly 1 display card of your choice, regardless of reputation; no deck draw occurs. 3. Cards II: advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order using the upgraded draw table. 4. Cards II snap begins at strength 3 and still takes exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation; reputation restrictions apply to the side-II draw option, not snapping. 5. Cards II display cards are not replenished until the turn is complete; after any turn taking display cards, compact higher folders downward in order and refill empty folders. 6. Hand size is unrestricted during a turn and checked only at breaks: 3 cards normally, or 5 with the hand-limit university.
answers.evidence: Cards action: both sides advance Break 2; I snap at 5+, II snap at 3; display not replenished until turn complete; hand limit checked at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. “Within reputation range” means the display folder matching your Reputation counter plus all lower-numbered folders. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action; Cards II unlocks progress past 9. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter: gain 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display defines range; reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; on 15 further reputation converts to appeal; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building, size no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but never two identical buildings in that action. 2. Pay 2 money per space, separately before placing each building (size × 2). 3. The first building must have at least one space on a border space; every later building must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Buildings must fit on empty map spaces, remain on the map, and not cover rock or water. 4. Spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5. Each new kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, once per pavilion.
answers.evidence: Build action table and placement rules specify side limits, 2 money per space, first-building border rule, restricted spaces, kiosk spacing, and pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo; Reptile Houses and Large Bird Aviaries require Build II. 2. Each special enclosure type has four physical tiles in the shared supply, and an individual zoo may have at most one Petting Zoo, one Reptile House, and one Large Bird Aviary. 3. Unique buildings cannot be built with the Build action; they enter through their Sponsor cards. 4. If every zoo-map space except water and rock is covered, immediately gain 7 appeal; this may also be triggered by effects other than Build.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table; each individual zoo may contain only one of each special enclosure; unique buildings only via Sponsors; full map grants 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Yes, benefits earned earlier in an action—including money, cards, and newly activated workers—may be used for later steps of that same action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefit. 2. Thus an earlier money bonus may pay for a later building or animal, and an earlier task may provide a worker for a later task in the same Association II action, but a bonus from a step cannot pay that step’s own cost. 3. Immediate effects resolve during the action; effects labeled “after finishing” wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. 4. When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure permits earlier action bonuses for later steps and requires paying each item before its own benefits; Association II allows earlier worker bonuses; simultaneous effects order is chosen by owner.

answers.answer: 1. Before playing each Animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its full printed cost, and house it legally. A matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on that animal card, so a double icon reduces it by 6. Money gained from the play itself comes later and cannot fund that animal’s cost. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal’s printed minimum size; any animal except a Petting Zoo animal can use it, and the entire enclosure is flipped to its occupied side. 3. Petting Zoo animals can only live in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may instead use their indicated Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary spaces; add one supply player token for each required space, and never flip a special enclosure. 4. Meet water/rock adjacency requirements at the chosen enclosure, including special enclosures; count distinct adjacent hexes, not repeated edges touching one hex. 5. Resolve ordinary effects immediately before playing the next animal; “after finishing” effects wait until all animals and the Action-card move are complete. For two animals, finish the first animal’s steps before the second; the second may be declined.
answers.evidence: Animals I steps: conditions, cost, housing, card, effects; partner discount is 3 per continent icon; terrain adjacency applies to chosen housing; “after finishing” effects wait.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II allows Animal cards from the display within your reputation range, in addition to hand cards; the two animals allowed at strength 5+ may be any mix of hand and display. 2. Pay an additional cost equal to the display folder number for each display animal. 3. At strength 5 or more, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, before choosing animals, so the increased range applies to that action. 4. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 5. Animals II permits playing animals with an upgrade-required condition.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display within range with folder cost; optional reputation first at strength 5+; display not replenished until turn end; may play upgrade-conditioned animals.

answers.answer: 1. Relocation is allowed only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, once per new building; move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing separately for each animal. The summary does not give a fixed maximum count beyond the available eligible animals and capacity. 2. For each moved animal, remove it from its standard enclosure and put the required number of supply player tokens on free spaces in the new special enclosure. The special enclosure must meet that animal’s terrain needs and have enough capacity. 3. Empty the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all of that animal’s requirements, including water/rock. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none. 4. Special enclosures are not flipped; the new animal tokens mark occupied capacity.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals: only immediately when a Reptile House/Aviary is built; relocate all eligible animals that fit; choose each separately; use smallest enclosure meeting requirements with stated fallback.

answers.answer: 1. The Association tasks and strengths are: increase reputation, 2; gain partner zoo, 3; gain university, 4; conservation project work, 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task and needs at least one active worker; the action strength must be at least the task strength. Association II performs one or more different tasks, with total task value no greater than action strength; each task uses 1 or 2 workers under the repeat rule. 3. If one of your workers is already on a task, you must place 2 workers there; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot do that task again until after the break. 4. Other players’ workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association I task list states values and worker repetition rules; Association II permits different tasks whose total value does not exceed strength.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from the available tiles on the Association board, then place them on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; take any printed covered-space bonus immediately. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must represent different continents and you may have at most 4. The third and fourth partner zoos require Association II. 3. When taking a university, resolve both its covered-space bonus and its own reputation award immediately. Universities provide research icons; the hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5. Other universities leave it at 3. 4. Partner zoos reduce animal costs by 3 money per matching continent icon and provide their continent icon. The Association board restocks one tile of each type at breaks, except kinds already owned by every player; it does not add duplicate available tiles.
answers.evidence: Association tasks: take tiles from board to lowest available map space; partner limits/bonuses; university tile reputation and hand-limit effects; break restocking rules.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. With Association II, the new project may instead come from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number; it is not replenished until turn end. 2. To enter play, put the new card in the leftmost space above the Association board and push existing cards right. The base projects below the board never move and are never replenished. 3. To support, fulfill a printed condition and choose an available reward level with no token from any player; a project may normally be supported only once by you, even if another level is open. Take one player token from the left edge of your zoo map and place it on the chosen condition. 4. Gain the depicted conservation/reputation and activate the uncovered map bonus. Resolve the project reward and immediate map bonus in either order; recurring-income map bonuses are also taken now and at every later break. 5. The above-board project limit is 2, 3, or 4 cards depending on player count (3 in a three-player game). If adding a card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost project; return its tokens to their owners’ supplies, while their map bonuses remain active.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work explains entry sources, support limits and token, map bonus timing, overflow, and token return.

answers.answer: 1. For a Release into the Wild project, the animal’s printed standard-enclosure requirement must match the depicted size category: 2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts exactly size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. The actual occupied enclosure or special-enclosure capacity does not determine the category. 2. Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal’s printed appeal and discard it, losing its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. 3. If it could live in a special enclosure and the required special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all animal requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone if none meets all; if none meets size, flip none. This applies to flock animals too. 4. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting an already-played one does not.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild paragraph specifies exact printed size bands, lost/retained effects, special-token priority, enclosure fallback, and new-card reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand; action strength must be at least its level and all conditions must be met. Its other option advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money, even if fewer steps remain before the last space. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more Sponsors from hand and/or display within reputation range. Its strength plus 1 must be at least the sum of levels; X-tokens can raise strength above 5. Pay each display card’s folder number as an extra cost; replenish display only at turn end. 3. Resolve cards sequentially, fully completing each card’s immediate effects before the next; defer “after finishing” effects until the action is done. 4. If Sponsors II instead chooses the Break-token money option, take money twice the action strength, even when only one step remains before the last space.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I/II specify levels, sources and folder cost, order and delayed effects; money options pay full amount (II twice).

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens; recall association workers and restock eligible partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is 3 cards normally or 5 with the hand-limit university, and is checked only at breaks. 3. For each kiosk, take 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do. Adjacency means sharing at least one side. 4. If multiple players receive display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise beginning with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise); after each such player’s income, refill the display before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure enumerates steps and income; kiosk income lists qualifying neighbors; display-card break income is clockwise with refill after each affected player.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or one Bonus tile at that space; use it immediately and remove it, while the money choice remains if tiles are gone. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check for the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters occupy the same scoring area or pass one another. If you gain appeal during another player’s turn, the receiving zoo owner waits until the end of their own turn or a break to check. 3. If triggered at the end of a player’s turn, that player finishes and everyone else takes one more turn. If triggered during a break, everyone takes one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 conservation points. If nobody reaches 10 conservation before game end, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring. 5. Find the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; Victory Points equal your Appeal minus that Target Number. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with the most supported conservation projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory sections specify milestones, end-check timing, last turns, 4-point cap, VP formula and tie rules.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place one face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8. Do not put tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons; return the other five tiles to the box. 2. Component supply quantity does not itself forbid a legal play: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup says shuffle 9 tiles, place on four blank spaces, return five; component supply says use a suitable substitute if stock runs out.

answers.answer: 1. Advanced maps are reverse sides Maps 1–8. Choose 1 of 2 random zoo maps, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse play order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; its printed kiosk counts as built, and a kiosk tile is placed over it as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A gives advanced-map selection methods and Map A’s starting enclosure/kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. Put the seven player tokens used for conservation support on the designated spaces along the left edge of each player’s zoo map; keep the rest of the player tokens in supply. 2. When hiring workers, activate them from the lowest reserve space upward. 3. If a zoo map grants conservation points for hiring the last worker, take that reward when the last worker is activated.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2 places 7 tokens at left edge; Association worker supply says hire lowest upward and certain maps grant conservation when hiring last worker.

answers.answer: 1. Flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II when you gain an upgrade; it stays in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is usable from your next action, while the card immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. You cannot upgrade all five cards: there are four upgrade opportunities, and one allows an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: stays in slot, side-II action from next action, immediately counts as upgraded for conditions; four ways mean not all cards can be upgraded.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draw/discard amounts by strength are: strength 1, 1 draw/1 discard; 2, 1/0; 3, 2/1; 4, 2/0; 5 or more, 3/1. 2. Any required discard may be either a card just drawn or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw table gives side-I draw/discard counts; text says required discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. The animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bears remain a category even when combined with herbivore or predator icons; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Include both special categories when an effect asks for animal categories unless it explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: seven animal categories include bear and Petting Zoo animal unless explicitly excluded.

answers.answer: 1. A donation is Association II only; Association must be upgraded, and you must have performed at least one Association task in the same action. It uses no worker and is limited to one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible and cover that space with a player token from your supply; gain 1 conservation point. Skip spaces blocked at setup. 3. Cost ladder is 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12. Once all but the final space are covered, every later donation costs 12 and places no further token.
answers.evidence: Donations—Association II only states eligibility, one-per-action, payment/token/reward, ladder, blocked spaces, and repeatable final space.

answers.answer: 1. Count upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards. Count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or conservation-project icons; a university’s reputation award and hand-limit symbol are not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo lists included and excluded icons; card counts own icons; doubled icons count twice; “Card text takes priority.”

answers.answer: 1. For a two-water or two-rock requirement, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; several edges touching the same hex count as only one. In a larger water/rock area, count only hexes actually adjacent to the chosen enclosure. 2. Connectedness of a terrain region does not make nonadjacent hexes count. 3. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not satisfy requirements.
answers.evidence: Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; multiple edges touching one hex count once; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild Conservation Project card grants 1 reputation; later supporting a release project already in play does not grant that play bonus. 2. For every Breeding Program project card (123–127), the same condition applies at all three reward spaces on that card; if you meet it, choose any available reward space. This includes the Reptile Breeding Program example.
answers.evidence: Release-project paragraph distinguishes new play from support; ALL Breeding Program project cards use same requirement across all three spaces and any available reward.

answers.answer: 1. In an effect written X:Y, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2. A condition with no number, or one marked “per,” pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds are listed, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: X left is condition/Y right reward; unnumbered or per conditions pay once per fulfillment; numbered thresholds pay once and highest met applies.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map, and personal supply. 5. “Any zoo” includes those areas for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary defines connected, isolated, border space, your zoo, and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings enter play through their Sponsor cards and must be placed as part of playing the Sponsor; if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. 2. Pay no size-based construction cost. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip it. Follow ordinary placement rules and the building’s water/rock adjacency requirement. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house animals, and never count as terrain spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique-building glossary says place when playing Sponsor, otherwise card cannot be played; matching tile, rotate but not flip; ordinary placement/terrain; no size cost.

answers.answer: 1. For either a Named Action or Determination, first finish the Animals action, including moving the Animals card to slot 1; then use the granted action’s own Action card normally and move that card to slot 1 after the granted action. 2. Named Action specifies the action and cannot be replaced with the X-token alternative. 3. Determination (Any Action) lets you choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications give shared timing and movement; Named Action excludes replacement; Determination includes any action including X-token.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion takes a chosen project from the unused face-down base-project deck; Dominance takes its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if that named project is already in play. 3. Later play the acquired card through Association and immediately support it; place it above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below it.
answers.evidence: Assertion/Dominance clarification says search unused face-down base-project deck; Dominance does nothing if in play; later play and support above board.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing the Animals action and moving that Action card. 2. Clever puts the chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost/Clever clarification states after-finishing timing, chosen slot, and card-shifting directions.

answers.answer: 1. An affected zoo must have at least 5 appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering, or Venom. The playing animal’s appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when choosing affected players. 2. Venom affects every other eligible zoo with higher appeal than yours; you are never a target. Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation; you are never a target. 3. Hypnosis targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo, with the actor choosing among tied leaders; it has no effect if the actor is that target, and only slots 1–3 may be copied. 4. Pilfering 1 targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo and an eligible most-conservation zoo, with the conservation target needing at least 1 conservation. The actor chooses tied leaders; a self-target selection has no effect. 5. For multiplayer groups preferring not to use interactive abilities, the cards’ marked solo replacement text may be used without playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities section establishes 5-appeal floor, target rules, self-targets, timing note, and optional replacement text.

answers.answer: 1. Each affected other zoo puts Constriction tokens on its own Action cards. Ahead on one track: one token on its slot-5 card; ahead on both tracks: one token on each of its slot-4 and slot-5 cards. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return the token after acting or without effect at the next break.
answers.evidence: Constriction details specify affected zoo’s own cards, slots 4/5, no stacking, −2 strength, multiplied actions, and removal timing.

answers.answer: 1. A Constriction-marked card in slot 1 or 2 can have effective strength zero or less. To use it as a regular action, spend enough X-tokens to reach strength 1. 2. Alternatively, use the X-token action, or leave the card until it reaches at least slot 3. The X-token alternative is allowed despite Constriction, provided you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Constriction rule: at zero or below, boost to at least one, use alternative X-token action, or wait until slot 3; X-token action is available below cap.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between its two options, and you decide again after each card, so the second choice may differ from the first. 2. A discarded display card through Digging is replaced immediately: higher folders slide down and a deck card fills folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarifies choose up to twice and decide again after each; display card is replaced immediately with folders shifted and folder 6 filled.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal avoids occupying a new enclosure only if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal’s standard-enclosure size. 2. That same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals; it need not itself be a flock animal. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. No proof of the flock animal’s historical accommodation is needed when releasing it; release follows the usual procedure and frees an occupied enclosure under that procedure even if it originally shared.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification states host condition, unlimited reuse, later non-flock restriction, and release frees an enclosure without tracking historical residents.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for hiring your last worker. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated: activate lowest remaining reserve worker; take last-worker conservation reward; no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards and adds one revealed Animal card to your hand, discarding all the others. If none is an Animal, discard all revealed cards and add nothing.
answers.evidence: Hunter X clarification states keep one revealed Animal and discard the rest; if none is an Animal, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis chooses a highest-appeal eligible player, with the actor deciding among ties; it has no effect if the actor is the target. Only a target card in slot 1, 2, or 3 may be chosen. 2. The copied action uses the target card’s upgraded or unupgraded side for the entire action; other upgrade checks use your own Action cards. You may spend your own X-tokens. 3. Venom and Constriction on the copied card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally. 4. Borrowed Build II permits its special enclosures and restricted spaces; borrowed Animals II permits upgrade-conditioned animals; borrowed Association I keeps its two-partner limit. A unique building played through borrowed Sponsors checks your own Build side.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification specifies tied/self target, eligible slots, target side, own X-tokens, tokens/multiplier, card movement, and borrowed-action exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. If a reward names an Action card, put its Multiplier on that card; a Bonus tile lets you choose any Action card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, the action may be executed twice in succession at the same base strength; move the Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer “after finishing” effects until all executions are complete. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn ends; it does not stop the second execution. 4. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; remove an unused token during the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier table and rules state placement, double execution, X-token scope, timing and return; break waits until entire turn finished.

answers.answer: 1. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution, so two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. 2. You may spend X-tokens on a multiplied card; each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. You cannot mix an X-token alternative execution with a regular action execution; a multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token holding limit.
answers.evidence: Multiplier choices: each additional token adds one execution; X-tokens boost one; may not mix X-token action with regular; multiplied X-token alternative may take two.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking allows you to place a Large Bird Aviary before upgrading Build, but only if your zoo does not already have one and there is a legal site. 2. Other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for restricted-icon map spaces. 3. Place multiple buildings from Posturing one at a time under normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing; resolve the successive building placements sequentially.
answers.evidence: Peacocking clarification allows pre-upgrade Aviary subject to no existing Aviary/legal site and retains restrictions; Posturing uses normal rules, sequentially.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animals give 3 appeal for the first, 6 for the second, and 9 for the third. 2. The single Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification gives 3/6/9 appeal, maximum three, and classifies them as small.

answers.answer: 1. For both Pilfering 1 and each target selection of Pilfering 2, the acting player chooses among tied leaders. 2. Pilfering 2’s conservation-target part requires a leader with at least 1 conservation. If all players have zero conservation, that part has no effect, but its separate highest-appeal target still resolves if eligible. 3. A self-target selection has no effect; for Pilfering 2, resolve the other selection normally.
answers.evidence: Pilfering clarification: actor chooses ties for both abilities; zero-conservation part has no effect; self-target has no effect and other selection still resolves.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money; if they have less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilferings one at a time; the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X details target choice and fallback for no cards, insufficient money, neither resource, and sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch lets you tuck up to X hand cards under the animal for 2 appeal each; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard those tucked cards too, but keep the appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing lets you sell up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch and Sunbathing clarifications specify tucked/sold card destinations and retained appeal.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins your choices when you discard one card at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card is individually subject to its own maximum of 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance: extra card before milestone joins choices when discarding one; score every remaining card, each with four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down and draws the stated number of cards at random. Make the ability’s stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. For Scavenging 3, draw three random cards, keep one, and discard the others.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification gives random face-down draw, selection, and return face up; illustrated Scavenging 3 keeps one of three.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. If no eligible result is available for an ability, it has no effect. 2. Sponsor Magnet finds display Sponsors without a reputation-range restriction; if no Sponsor is present, nothing happens. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification specifies exact card source, no reputation restriction for Sponsor Magnet, empty result, and ordinary refill.

answers.answer: 1. Place Venom tokens on the affected player’s lowest-slot Action cards first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; return duplicates to supply. 2. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn. This includes using the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token during that turn and at least one Venom token remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money does not avoid the fee. 4. Unused Venom tokens clear at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom rules specify slot placement/no stacking, removal on use, fee condition and inability fallback, and break clearing.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives immediate money based on universities: 2 for 1 university, 5 for 2, or 10 for 3. 2. It reduces the strength required for conservation project work from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, Veterinarian 203: immediate 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities; task strength 4; final 1 conservation for three.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough’s immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported conservation project, counted by the player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map. 2. At each break it gives 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Medical Breakthrough 206 immediate reward counts missing left-map tokens; break reward is 1 conservation.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research totals the different continent and animal-category icon types in your zoo; research icons are excluded. Count each type once despite multiple or doubled copies. 2. Its owner gains 1 conservation per two types, rounding down. 3. Each other player gains 2 money per conservation point the owner gains.
answers.evidence: Basic Research 207 states included/different types and excludes research; one conservation per two; others get 2 money per point.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player—including the owner—plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Science Library 208 lists immediate appeal, owner reward on any player’s research icon, and final five-category condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon when played. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules, including the requirement that kiosks be at least 3 spaces from other kiosks. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: Expert on the Americas 210 lists immediate appeal per icon, free kiosk under normal rules, and five-kiosk final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon when played. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Expert on Australia 212: immediate appeal per icon; per icon may tuck one hand card for 2 appeal, with no remaining function.

answers.answer: 1. When played, Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program each take 2 player tokens from your supply and put them on that Sponsor’s two printed top spaces. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly 1 token from this card to your supply as one icon. You cannot use both tokens from the same card for one project. Base-origin project cards later played above the board do not qualify. 3. The final-scoring condition grants 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing tokens at the left edge of your zoo map.
answers.evidence: 215/218 reference specifies two stored tokens, one substitute icon per base-below-board support, no double use, excludes base-origin cards above board, and final support condition.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without additional strength; pay its normal money cost and follow placement rules. 2. Only one extra building is allowed, even if the action builds several different buildings. Special enclosures remain limited to one of each type per zoo. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map except water and rock.
answers.evidence: Engineer 217 specifies one extra copy, no extra strength, normal payment/placement and special-enclosure limits; final 5 appeal for full map.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It permits covering water/rock map spaces and ignoring terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist, and Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for a full map. 4. At final scoring, gain 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to 3 pairs (maximum 6 appeal).
answers.evidence: Diversity Researcher 219 lists immediate reward, terrain permission/ignored requirements and counting exceptions, and final pairs/cap.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers whenever an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. For each such trigger, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border; it can be the same bonus selected by another trigger or a different one. Resolve bonuses in the order you choose. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: Archaeologist 221 states border placement trigger, any uncovered bonus, repeated/same choices and final border-space condition.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but place at most one token on that project per Association action. 3. Each placed token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Migration Recording 224 immediate X-token; additional conservation per release support; repeated support, one token per project per action, each counts separately.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It grants immunity to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis, and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and select the next qualifying player instead. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation with all five continents.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Lab 225 lists X-token, immunities/redirect, and all-five-continents final reward.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Special Assignment permanently chooses small or large; mark the chosen box with a supply player token. Reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that chosen size, keep it, and discard the others. 2. Thereafter, only the chosen type may be played: the opposite type is prohibited. 3. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal each; chosen large animals gain 4. Size-3 animals remain legal but gain no bonus.
answers.evidence: WAZA Special Assignment 227 describes permanent type, search, prohibition, and small/large/size-3 results.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal when played. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals qualifies; it lets you play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs and rules. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to your hand regardless of reputation. You may take the display animal even if you declined the additional play. Mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents the effect.
answers.evidence: WAZA Small Animals Program 228 gives money, only-small action condition, extra hand animal, and display animal without reputation restriction.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon when played. 2. Its recurring effect gives 1 money for each space newly covered adjacent to water, even if multiple spaces are in one building; a space beside several water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final condition grants 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected, meaning none is isolated.
answers.evidence: Hydrologist 241 lists immediate reward, per newly covered space money, and all-water-connected final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is played with its unique building, following the general unique-building placement rules. 2. Each bird icon played draws 2 deck cards; keep 1 and discard the other.
answers.evidence: Barred Owl Hut 249 says place unique building and each bird icon played draws two deck cards, keep one, discard other; no terrain requirement is stated.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is a unique building placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to 2 hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.
answers.evidence: Sea Turtle Tank 250: place adjacent to water; per reptile icon may sell up to two hand cards for four money each and discard them.

answers.answer: 1. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with a number of draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. A newly played card with two predator icons triggers two Hunters sequentially; the total predator count includes both new icons for each trigger.
answers.evidence: Spotted Hyena Compound 252: Hunter draws equal total predator icons; double-predator card triggers twice, counting both new icons each time.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable places its building and 3 supply tokens on its Sponsor card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor’s level to play that Sponsor, meeting its normal conditions. 3. The Sponsor must come from hand; the card’s own herbivore icon can trigger this effect when Okapi Stable itself is played. There are three total uses.
answers.evidence: Okapi Stable 253 gives three tokens; per herbivore may spend token and pay hand Sponsor level with conditions; own icon can trigger; three uses.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation immediately. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Then take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card; resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Zoo School 254 immediate track rewards, at least two border spaces, card choices, and chosen order for simultaneous benefits.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance’s unique building may cover two border spaces and need not touch an existing building; other placement rules apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break, it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may stand beside a kiosk. 3. Because it is a unique building, adjacent kiosks count it for their income. 4. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: Side Entrance 257 gives two-border-space placement exception, future attachment, income per adjacent building, kiosk interaction, and final reward.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space immediately; water and rock spaces never count. 2. At final scoring, gain 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately and rounding down within each group. 3. Restricted/upgrade-marked spaces count as empty building spaces even if Build is not upgraded; terrain spaces do not count.
answers.evidence: Native Farm Animals 260 describes border spaces, excludes terrain, scores each contiguous group by six, and includes restricted spaces.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon type immediately; research icons do not count. 2. Its recurring effect grants 1 appeal and 2 money whenever a category or continent type is newly introduced to your zoo. A double of the same new icon is one new type, so it grants the novelty reward only once.
answers.evidence: Explorer 262 immediate money counts different types excluding research; new category/continent yields appeal and money; double identical type only once.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place one size-5 standard enclosure free, following normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, it lets you ignore one left-side condition, such as a required icon or Animals upgrade; it does not ignore terrain requirements. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: WAZA Large Animal Program 263 gives free size-5 enclosure and ignores one condition except terrain; stacks with Research Institute to ignore two.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares animal-category icon counts in your zoo with the player to your right; gain 1 conservation for each category where your count is higher. 2. If that player has no icons of a category, one of yours is enough to be higher. 3. The maximum is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Biodiverse Zoo 009 counts categories with more icons than player to right; one icon beats none; maximum four.

answers.answer: 1. Map 1 Observation Tower benefits only standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not enclosures merely adjacent to another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. If an animal is housed there after an earlier animal was released, the two appeal are gained again. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 clarification specifies tower-hex adjacency, standard enclosures only, repeat after release/refill, and not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Map 2 Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. That standard enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. 3. The size increase cannot be ignored on release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and the Outdoor Area is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 clarification states qualifying hex, +2 size for all purposes, no ignoring on release/transfer, no special-enclosure effect, not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Map 4 Commercial Harbor is activated when a building occupies its adjacent building space; your first building may start there but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used only once per own turn, before, during, or after your action; not during breaks or another player’s turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 clarification states activation, first-building option, timing and once-per-turn restriction, and not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Map 5 Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, not per building; empty enclosures count, and each hex of a multi-hex building counts separately. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and contributes zero income to adjacent kiosks; those kiosks still count other qualifying neighbors. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, your choice, even before Build II. It does not give both, and other normal placement rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Map 5 clarification defines per-hex income and empty enclosures; Restaurant not a building for kiosk income; free choice of one special enclosure before Build II.

answers.answer: 1. On Map 8 Hollywood Hills, cover each H space by placing a building under ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep that Sponsor and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor’s level is one lower. 4. Upgrade restrictions remain: bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II for restricted-icon spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 clarification states cover/build, reveal-to-Sponsor, not placement bonus, level reduction, and continuing upgrade restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. For the bonus that pays money to play a Sponsor, pay money equal to that Sponsor’s level and meet its normal play conditions. 2. Play it only from your hand, even if Sponsors II is upgraded; a display card is not allowed. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ: paid-Sponsor effect costs level, requires usual conditions, hand only even with Sponsors II, and leaves Sponsors card in current slot.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond those track ends are lost.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: appeal cannot exceed 113, nor conservation 41; gains beyond ends are lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, provided each has at least 5 appeal; you are never a target. 2. Hypnosis targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo, with the actor choosing among ties; it has no effect if the actor is the target and may copy only slots 1, 2, or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets an eligible highest-appeal zoo and a most-conservation zoo with at least 1 conservation. The actor chooses tied leaders for each selection; self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead on appeal and/or conservation. Ahead on one track gets one token on that target’s slot-5 card; ahead on both gets one token on each of its slot-4 and slot-5 cards.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and subsequent detailed clauses give each selection, tie/self rules, Hypnosis slots, appeal floor, and Constriction token counts.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from the continent shown on the Animal card. A Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition permits any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-appeal condition means you may play the card only while your appeal is 25 or less; the marker is only a reminder, not a general cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation value. 4. A minus-one-condition bonus ignores one requirement on the card’s left edge; all other conditions still apply, and terrain requirements cannot be waived.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ specifies Animal/Sponsor partner conditions, max-25 and minimum reputation, and −1 condition effect excluding terrain waiver.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine’s Digging 2 permits up to two selections. Each selection may be either discard a display card and replenish it, or discard a hand card and draw one deck card. 2. You choose again after each card, so the two selections need not use the same option.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: choose up to twice between display discard/refill or hand discard/deck draw; decide again after each card.

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken, move remaining cards from higher-numbered folders down into gaps while preserving their order, then fill empty folders from the deck. 2. During a break specifically, discard folders 1 and 2, move remaining cards down in order, and refill; during break income, refill after each player who takes a display card.
answers.evidence: Display timing says move cards from higher folders down, keeping order, and fill empty spaces; break procedure discards folders 1–2 and refills.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures with the empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus space covered is awarded immediately once, before the next building; later flipping the enclosure to its occupied side does not award those bonuses again.
answers.evidence: Build action: standard enclosure empty side up; covered placement bonuses gained immediately once and not again when occupied.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, every player chooses and discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation track 10-point milestone: all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turn order proceeds clockwise. 2. The game does not use formal rounds: players take turns one at a time until the end is triggered, with breaks as administration phases between turns. 3. On a normal turn, perform one action using one of the five Action cards. Resolve any action effects and then move the used card; after-finishing effects occur after that movement. Some actions may contain multiple steps or additional effects, but the turn’s selected regular Action card action is one action.
answers.evidence: Setup randomly determines start player and clockwise order; Overview says no formal rounds; Turn Structure says one action per turn and defines after-finishing timing.

answers.answer: 1. If nobody reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: Conservation track 10-point milestone says if no one reaches 10 before game end, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins; orientation/destination are not stated there.
